mcq.QUESTION_DESC: What is the recommended approach to handle SQL exceptions in JDBC code?
Which block is best suited for closing JDBC resources like Connection, Statement, and ResultSet?
Which Java feature simplifies closing JDBC resources automatically?
What will happen if you don’t close the ResultSet and Connection after query execution?
In JDBC, which exception is thrown when a query fails due to invalid SQL syntax?

sq.ANSWER:
A Java feature that auto-closes resources implementing AutoCloseable.
Example:

try (Connection con = DriverManager.getConnection(...)) 
{ // use connection } 
catch (SQLException e) 
{ e.printStackTrace(); 
}
sq.QUESTION_DESC: What is try-with-resources? Give an example of its use in JDBC.

sq.ANSWER: The finally block ensures that resources like Connection, Statement, and ResultSet are closed regardless of whether an exception occurs or not, preventing memory/resource leaks.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: What is the purpose of the finally block in JDBC resource handling?

lq.ANSWER:
import java.sql.*;

public class EmployeeData {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String url = "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/company";
        String user = "root";
        String pass = "admin";
        
        Connection con = null;
        Statement stmt = null;
        ResultSet rs = null;

        try {
            // Load Driver
            Class.forName("com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver");

            // Establish Connection
            con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass);

            // Create Statement
            stmt = con.createStatement();

            // Execute Query
            rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT name, salary FROM employees");

            // Process Results
            while (rs.next()) {
                System.out.println("Name: " + rs.getString("name") +
                                   ", Salary: " + rs.getDouble("salary"));
            }

        } catch (SQLException e) {
            System.err.println("Database error: " + e.getMessage());
        } catch (ClassNotFoundException e) {
            System.err.println("Driver not found: " + e.getMessage());
        } finally {
            // Close resources
            try { if (rs != null) rs.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
            try { if (stmt != null) stmt.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
            try { if (con != null) con.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
        }
    }
}
